title: Dynamical resource theory of time-reversal symmetry breaking
authors: Jisho Miyazaki, Kohdai Kuroiwa, Mio Murao
abstract: Time-reversal symmetry and its violation (T-violation) are fundamental across diverse physics domains, from particle physics to fluctuation theorems and reciprocity. While time-reversal symmetry for isolated systems is simply determined by the Hamiltonian, quantifying the magnitude of T-violation, especially in noisy quantum processes, has been a subject of ongoing debate. Here, we propose an operationally meaningful framework to quantify the intrinsic T-violation of quantum channels. We integrate operationally defined time-reversal transformations into dynamical resource theory to formulate T-violation as a resource. T-violation decomposes into two distinct components: kinematic T-violation originating from antiunitary motion-reversal, and nonunitality driven purely by thermodynamics. This decomposition resolves the longstanding confusion between broken time-reversal symmetry and non-invertibility. Finally, we analyze the resulting resource theory of kinematic T-violation, showing that it is neither quality-like nor quantity-like, and proving the existence of a universal golden unit even within classical channels.
summary: This paper introduces a dynamical resource theory to quantify time-reversal symmetry breaking in general quantum channels. It resolves a long-standing ambiguity by decomposing total T-violation into a thermodynamic component (nonunitality) and a kinematic component. This framework provides a powerful, operational measure for studying symmetry breaking in open quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop an operationally meaningful framework to quantify intrinsic Time-reversal symmetry breaking (T-violation) in general quantum channels, resolving the conceptual confusion between T-violation and non-invertibility.
main_result: T-violation is decomposed into two distinct, additive components: kinematic T-violation (from antiunitary motion-reversal) and nonunitality driven by thermodynamics. The resource theory of kinematic T-violation is shown to be robust and applicable even to classical channels.
method: The authors employ dynamical resource theory, defining T-symmetry operationally for quantum channels and decomposing the total T-violation into its constituent parts using specific antiunitary operators.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed on general quantum channels ($\mathcal{E}$), extending beyond simple Hamiltonians to account for non-unitary, dissipative processes. The framework uses concepts like motion-reversal operators ($\Theta$) and the Oreshkov–Cerf formalism.
key_observables: T-violation, kinematic T-violation, nonunitality, transition probabilities, and resource measures like trace distance and relative entropy.
important_parameters: The decomposition relies on the relationship $	ext{T-violation} = 	ext{nonunitality} + 	ext{kinematic T-violation}$.
main_assumptions: The definition of motion reversal is relative to a chosen reference time displacement ($U_{\Delta t}$), and the analysis focuses on the simplest setting without decomposing into superselection sectors.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically relates original and motion-reversed processes for a system with momentum. Figure 5 shows the correspondence between process theory elements and quantum circuit elements.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the operational definition of T-symmetry for processes, then develops the resource theory framework by decomposing T-violation, and finally analyzes the resulting resource theory of kinematic T-violation.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, operational tool to quantify fundamental symmetries in open quantum systems, which is crucial for understanding decoherence and non-equilibrium dynamics in AMO physics.
